column2: Sweets and sugar. Candy, cakes, and sugary drinks. Sweets often contain a lot of added sugar. Have them less often and in smaller portions.
Dairy foods. Milk, yogurt, and cheese. Dairy foods can provide calcium and protein. Choose a variety that suits your needs.
Meat and eggs. Chicken, meat, and eggs. Meat and eggs provide protein and other nutrients. Cook them thoroughly.
Fish. Fish and seafood. Fish provides protein, and some types contain omega-three fatty acids.
Fruit. Apples, bananas, oranges, and other fruits. Fruit provides fiber, vitamins, and water. Wash it before eating.
Apples, bananas, oranges, and other fruits.
Vegetables. Carrots, broccoli, tomatoes, and other vegetables. Eat vegetables of different colors. They provide fiber, vitamins, and minerals.
Carrots, broccoli, tomatoes, and other vegetables.
Grains. Bread, oats, rice, and pasta. Grains give us energy. Choose whole-grain options when possible.
Legumes. Beans, lentils, and chickpeas. Legumes contain plant protein and fiber. Cook them thoroughly before eating.
Nuts and seeds. Walnuts, almonds, and seeds. Nuts and seeds provide beneficial fats. Be aware of allergies and choking hazards for young children.
Water. Drinking water. Drink water regularly throughout the day. Needs vary with age, activity, and weather.
